newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan phosphates firm gets $161.2 mln loan.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan phosphates firm gets $161.2 mln loan.

text.p: Morocco's state-owned phosphates firm Office Cherifien des Phosphates (OCP) signed a one billion French francs ($161.2 million) investment accord with a group of French and Moroccan banks, an official said.

"This convention adds to the means already harnessed to implement investment programmes which total $1.3 billion for the period 1997-2002," Mourad Cherif, director-general, said during the signing ceremony in Morocco's financial centre, Casablanca.
The banks which are led by Societe Generale -Paris are Banque Nationale de Paris, la Banque Paribas, La Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur-Paris and Banque Commerciale du Maroc -Paris.
Cherif said OCP's objective was to increase by 30 percent its output potential on that period.
In 1996, phosphates exports reached 10.1 million tonnes for a turnover of $1.4 billion.
